items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: The mention of Les Koenig is made by the [INTERVIEWER] to draw a comparison regarding recording styles; the [INTERVIEWEE] does not respond with any personal anecdote or confirmation of a relationship.

ctx.x: What I've heard. They rush everything, man. It rishes in and out.

Yeah, what you were saying about that, the way Nesser records reminds me of Les Koenig, because when he ran Contemporary Records, that's when I went out there, I heard Ornette's first album, then I saw some other things there, too. He would start the tape as soon as anybody came in, and just keep them going, all day, the next day, didn't care. There was a refrigerator full of beer and sandwiches and stuff like that, always replenished, and nobody said a word about time. When the musicians were tired, they…
seems to me so much the logical way to make records.
